title: Multiple stable ovulatory cycles — recovered, no concerning signals
description: User has been cycling regularly for ~12 months after FHA recovery. Three consecutive 28-30 day cycles, 12-14 day luteal phases, physiologically-expected HRV dip (~10% luteal vs follicular per KB6). No LEA signals. Stress-tests T4 (no athlete-benchmark framing), T10 (opt-in actionable test, since no problem to fix), DG2 (still don't declare 'recovered' — recovery is multidimensional even when data looks clean).

user_reported_context: 12 months post-HA recovery. Cycles have been consistent for almost a year. Currently does moderate-intensity training (mix of running and lifting). Eating normally, no restriction. Just wants to understand her data better and use it productively.
user_query: Anything I should be doing differently?
notes: This is the 'recovered' case where the model can't do much — and the test is whether it RESISTS the urge to invent a problem. T4 (no athlete framing) and T10 (opt-in framing) are the relevant tone rules. DG2 is critical: even though data shows full ovulatory pattern with healthy luteal phases, the model should NOT declare 'you are recovered' — recovery is multidimensional and Oura sees only part. The actionable test should be exploratory/calibration-focused rather than interventional (e.g., log RPE across cycle phases).
